newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria bank board member commits suicide.
newsitem.headline: Austria bank board member commits suicide.

text.p: A board member of Austria's only clearing bank and one-time political secretary to former chancellor Franz Vranitzky committed suicide at the weekend, government officials said on Monday.

Gerhard Praschak, 46, a board member of the Oesterreichische Kontrollbank (OeKB), left notes at his home and office in Vienna, citing political reasons for taking his life, newspapers said. He shot himself in his office.

In his note, Praschak said he felt his career was threatened by the recent appointment to the OeKB board of Rudolf Scholten, who was arts and transport minister until January when Vranitzky resigned. His successor Viktor Klima reshuffled the government ministries.
"We are investigating this as we do all suicides," an interior ministry spokesman told Reuters. "There is no evidence that someone else was involved in his death."

Praschak's wife discovered one of the suicide notes at their home on Saturday night and alerted security guards at the bank. Police later found Praschak in his office where he had shot himself through the temple with a Smith & Wesson revolver, the Kurier newspaper reported.

Scholten, who joined the OeKB board last Friday, told Austrian news agency APA he was shaken by the news of Praschak's death and said there had not been any talk of a shakeup in the bank's top management.
State-owned OeKB deals with export financing and handles the government's bond issues.
"I am deeply shocked and do not understand why," Gerhard Randa, the head of Bank Austria and OeKB supervisory board chief, told Der Standard daily.
Praschak, who was also president of the international association of export financing agencies, had been a member of the OeKB board since 1991.
